options.misconception: No treaty recognized Wampanoag independence; the war ended with Metacom dead and his people scattered.

The English destroyed Native towns and food supplies across the region, and sold many survivors into slavery

rationales.A: No treaty recognized Wampanoag independence; the war ended with Metacom dead and his people scattered.
rationales.B: Earlier wars had been fought over a valley or a town; this one was fought everywhere at once, and the English waged it against the means of life itself. They burned villages, destroyed cornfields and food stores, and killed or captured so many people that the survivors could not rebuild. Metacom was killed in August 1676, and many of the captives were sold into slavery in the West Indies — a people can survive losing a battle, but not losing its towns, its food, and its people all at once.
rationales.C: The Wampanoag did not move west and rebuild; their power in New England was broken.
rationales.D: The French did not intervene; the war was fought between the English and Native peoples of New England.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the scale. Background: earlier wars were fought over a valley or a town; this one was fought everywhere at once.
2. Ask what was destroyed. Background: not just warriors, but villages, cornfields, and food stores — the means of life.
3. Count the outcome. Background: Metacom dead in August 1676, survivors sold into slavery, and a people unable to rebuild.
Remember: a people can survive losing a battle, but not losing its towns, its food, and its people at once.

stem: Unlike earlier conflicts in New England, King Philip's War ended Native power in the region. Which of the following best explains why this war, rather than earlier ones, had that result?

stimulus.text: An engraving by F. O. C. Darley, published in 1886 and captioned “The King Philip War — A Raid on the Settlers.” Native warriors carrying tomahawks and clubs attack settlers in a field; one settler fires a musket, a frightened child stands in the center, and a fallen settler lies in the foreground.
